claim_under_attack.capability_text: External validation of Hansen 3-component chi baseline on 8 canonical polymer-solvent chi values from published primary literature (Van Krevelen 1990 Table 7.6; Bawn 1949; Sakurada 1954; Krigbaum 1959; Malcolm-Rowlinson 1957). 5 polymers × 3 solvents. HONEST FINDING: Hansen predictions correlate STRONGLY (Pearson r=+0.8692) with experimental chi and 75% (6/8) predictions are within factor of 3, in contrast to my prior OMG-chi Hansen receipt which had catastrophic negative R² on DFT+COSMO-RS reference chi. This confirms Hansen theory IS useful for real polymer-solvent thermodynamics; the COSMO-RS reference in OMG is a different chi frame. Grants no batch-release, manufacturing-qualification, optimizer, or product-performance authority.

does_not_close: does not re-derive the Hansen delta_d/delta_p/delta_h values themselves (uses the KPI's own embedded per-pair predictions)
does not assert the 7 remaining literature citations are individually free of transcription error (only that they carry an author/year/source, unlike the flagged row)
does not extend coverage beyond the existing 8 pairs (Phase-1 already lists exactly this expansion as an awaiting item)
interpretation: One of the 8 rows counted toward this KPI's headline 'external validation ... on 8 canonical polymer-solvent chi values from published primary literature' claim (polystyrene/water, chi_published=3.5) is NOT sourced from any publication -- its own citation field reads 'Order-of-magnitude estimate; PS is hydrophobic, high chi'. Genuine literature coverage is 7/8, not 8/8. Recomputing the headline Pearson correlation with only the genuinely-literature-sourced 7 rows drops r from 0.8692 (p=0.0051, significant at alpha=0.05) to 0.6961 (p=0.0823), which is NOT significant at the conventional alpha=0.05 threshold. The leave-one-out sweep shows every OTHER single-row exclusion keeps p<0.02 -- significance is robust to removing any genuine literature point, and fails only when the one non-literature, self-estimated point is removed. The KPI's 'strong, validated' framing is therefore not a property of the 8 published values it claims to rest on; it is an artifact of including one self-authored guess in that count.

pre_registered_refutation_criteria.criterion_a: capability text claims '8 ... published primary literature' AND at least one row is not actually literature-sourced (no publication year, or self-disclosed as an 'estimate')
pre_registered_refutation_criteria.criterion_b: excluding the non-literature-sourced row(s) moves Pearson p from significant (p<0.05) to not-significant (p>=0.05)

rederivation_cross_check.note: the KPI text asserts correlation STRENGTH (r=0.8692) but never states or gates on a p-value / significance test; this audit adds that missing check.
